name: Rounded
subcategory: invoicing and tax for Australian sole traders
tagline: Invoicing, expense tracking and GST/BAS bookkeeping built specifically for Australian freelancers and sole traders.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible surface of Rounded is genuinely simple: clients, invoices, expenses, a GST column, a dashboard that tells you roughly what you owe. An agent can build that in a sitting, and the invoice PDF it produces will look fine. What it cannot build in a sitting is the boring half: live bank feeds, receipt capture that works on a phone, and tax logic that stays correct as ATO rules move. Rounded's real pitch is that an Australian sole trader can trust the BAS and income tax numbers without thinking, and a self-built ledger shifts that risk entirely onto you. Build it if your invoicing is simple and your accountant is patient; keep paying if the tax estimate is the reason you sleep at night.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you track clients, issue numbered invoices as PDFs, log expenses with GST flags from CSV bank imports, and see a quarterly GST and income summary.
requirements: Node 20+ and a local machine you actually back up
CSV exports from your bank, since there are no bank feeds
Your own ABN, logo and payment details for invoice templates
An accountant or the ATO portal for anything that gets lodged
whatYouLose: Automatic bank feeds and transaction matching, replaced by manual CSV imports
Mobile app for photographing receipts on the road
Tax rules that get updated for you when thresholds and rates change
Any path to lodging BAS or STP from inside the tool
Someone else's liability when the GST number is wrong
moatNotes: Australian tax specificity is the product. A generic invoicing app is a commodity; a tool that speaks BAS, GST and sole trader income tax to a non-accountant is not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because bookkeeping is a thing people pay to stop thinking about, and a DIY ledger reintroduces exactly the thinking they were paying to avoid. The monthly fee buys bank feeds that reconcile themselves, a tax estimate that updates as rules change, and a defensible export when an accountant or the ATO asks questions. Self-hosting your own books also means you are now the one responsible for backups, for GST edge cases like mixed-use expenses, and for noticing when a rate changed in July. For most sole traders the subscription costs less than one hour of accountant time per year.
notes: The invoicing half is a weekend; the tax confidence is the product you are actually buying.
prompt:
Build a local-first bookkeeping app for a single Australian sole trader. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via Drizzle ORM, and Playwright/Chromium for PDF rendering. Everything runs on localhost with `npm run dev`. Data lives in ./data/books.db.

Data model:
- business_profile: name, ABN, address, logo path, bank details, GST registered boolean, invoice number prefix and next number.
- clients: name, email, address, ABN, default payment terms in days.
- invoices: client, issue date, due date, status (draft, sent, paid), line items (description, qty, unit price, GST applicable boolean), notes. Store totals computed from line items: subtotal, GST total, grand total.
- expenses: date, supplier, description, amount including GST, GST amount, category, business use percentage, receipt file path.
- income_other: date, source, amount, GST amount, for money that did not come from an invoice.

Features in scope:
- CRUD screens for clients, invoices and expenses.
- Invoice PDF generation matching ATO tax invoice requirements: the words "Tax invoice", seller name and ABN, date, buyer details for invoices over 1000 AUD, line item GST, total GST payable.
- CSV bank statement import: upload a CSV, map columns interactively, then for each row let the user classify it as expense, invoice payment, or ignore. Remember supplier-to-category mappings for next time.
- Dashboard: money in, money out, outstanding invoices, and a GST summary per quarter (GST collected on sales minus GST credits on purchases) plus a rough taxable income figure.
- Quarterly summary export as CSV that an accountant can actually read.

Explicitly out of scope, and say so in the README: live bank feeds, BAS or STP lodgement, payroll, multi-currency, multi-user, anything that claims to be tax advice.

Seed the GST rate at 10 percent in a single config file, clearly marked as needing review. Store nothing in .env except the port and an optional basic-auth password. Include a `npm run backup` script that copies the SQLite file with a timestamp. README must include a blunt line that this tool computes estimates and does not replace an accountant.
